terms.gloss: it’s close now, we’re almost there
terms.grammar: prope as an adverb with est; jam “by now”
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 102: nam ad aedīs nostrās numquam adit, quamquam prope est
terms.comment: Plautus’s prope est is said of a place close by (the shrine of Good Fortune, next to the miser’s house); with jam it says that the place is close now. The sentence is ours: we have found no set phrase for “we’re almost there” in the authors we searched or in Traupman.

evidence: Verg. Ecl. 9.23: Tītyre, dum redeō (brevis est via), pāsce capellās
terms.comment: A herdsman’s words in a song: “till I come back (it’s a short way)”. See also it won’t be long.

phrases.latin: Jam prope est; vidēsne illud tēctum rubrum?
phrases.english: We’re almost there; do you see that red roof?

phrases.latin: Hinc adeō media est nōbīs via; namque sepulcrum incipit appārēre Biānoris.
phrases.english: From here on, you see, we are halfway; for Bianor’s tomb is beginning to come into view.

phrases.latin: nam ad aedīs nostrās numquam adit, quamquam prope est
phrases.english: for she never comes to our house, though she is close by
